::: {#exm-pue}

#### The datacenter that trained GPT-3

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
pue, kg_co2e_per_kwh = 1.10, 0.429
total_mwh = gpu_mwh * pue
tonnes_co2e = total_mwh * 1000 * kg_co2e_per_kwh / 1000
round_trips = tonnes_co2e / 180
print(total_mwh, tonnes_co2e, round_trips)
```

The datacenter where GPT-3 was trained had a [PUE](#def-pue) of `r sprintf("%.2f", py$pue)`,
according to the same table:
for each kilowatt-hour its computers used,
it used `r sprintf("%.2f", py$pue)` in all,
the rest going to cooling and power conversion.
The `r format(round(py$gpu_mwh), big.mark = ",")` megawatt-hours of @sol-gpt3-energy become `r format(round(py$total_mwh), big.mark = ",")` in all,
the figure @patterson2021carbon report.
At the `r py$kg_co2e_per_kwh` kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilowatt-hour that they use for United States electricity,
training emitted `r format(round(py$tonnes_co2e), big.mark = ",")` tonnes,
about `r sprintf("%.0f", py$round_trips)` times the 180 tonnes they give for a jet's round trip between San Francisco and New York.

:::
